title: Personality
examples: How much of my personality is from my parents?
Can I really change my personality?
What is the difference between nature and nurture?

explain.say: Today we will explore what makes you, you.
The Big Five model describes personality using five main traits.
Nature suggests that some traits are inherited from our genes.
Nurture means that our environment shapes who we become.

items: Culture and schooling matter a lot

explain.say: For example, a child raised in a very active family might become more outgoing.
Think about learning a new skill like playing the piano.

faq.q: Are the Big Five traits permanent?
faq.a: No, while they show tendencies, they can change over time. Life experiences and conscious effort can certainly influence your development.

faq.q: Does nature mean my parents decide who I am?
faq.a: Not exactly. Nature provides a starting range or predisposition, but it does not write your entire future for you. You still have free will.
asks: Is my personality just my genes?
How much control do my parents have?

faq.q: What is the difference between temperament and personality?
faq.a: Temperament refers to your basic, often observable emotional reactions, which are somewhat innate. Personality is the broader pattern of thoughts and feelings over time.

faq.q: If I score low on Openness, does that mean I am boring?
faq.a: No, it just means you might prefer routine or familiar things over constant novelty. There is nothing wrong with preferring what is comfortable.
asks: Does it mean I lack imagination?

faq.q: Can I use the Big Five to predict my job?
faq.a: It can suggest strengths, like pointing towards roles that match your natural tendencies. However, it is not a guaranteed predictor of your entire career path.
asks: Will this tell me what job to get?
Is it useful for career choices?

facts: The Big Five model includes Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism.
Nature refers to the biological inheritance passed down through genes.
Nurture refers to all the environmental influences, such as family and culture.
Personality is generally understood as a pattern of thinking and feeling.

quiz.say: A person who always plans ahead and finishes tasks on time shows high scores in which trait?
quiz.why: Conscientiousness relates to being organized and disciplined in your actions.

wrong.0: Agreeableness measures kindness, not planning ability.
wrong.1: Openness is about new ideas, not sticking to a plan.
wrong.3: Extraversion relates more to how outgoing you are, not how organized.

quiz.say: If a child is naturally very energetic and loves being around people, this is an example of:
quiz.why: Natural tendencies, like high energy, are often linked to genetic inheritance.

wrong.0: This option names a trait, not the source of the trait.
wrong.2: Nurture refers to learned behaviors from the environment.
wrong.3: This option names a trait, not the source of the trait.

quiz.say: A student who learns to share and cooperate with classmates is primarily developing which aspect of their personality?
quiz.why: Learning to share is a skill developed through social interaction and environment.

wrong.0: Openness relates to intellectual curiosity, not social sharing.
wrong.2: Neuroticism is about emotional reactions, not learned cooperation.
wrong.3: Nature describes inherited traits, not learned social skills.
